turns.text: can you make this less stiff? 'Dear Alex, Thank you for taking the time to speak with me yesterday regarding the role.' ugh
Try: 'Hi Alex — thanks for the conversation yesterday, I enjoyed hearing how the team actually ships.' Still a thank-you, less annual-review.
better. do I attach the one pager? feels thirsty
If they didn't ask, a link in the last line is lighter than an attachment. Attachment says 'please print me'.
link then. wait, they asked for it in the call. I forgot.
Then attach it, one file, filename that isn't FINAL_v7. Mention it in one sentence so it doesn't look like a stealth add.
k. the draft is still too long after the thanks.
Cut the paragraph about your 'passion for collaboration'. Keep one concrete thing you talked about.
we talked about oncall. I can say I'm not scared of it. that's dumb tho
Say you liked how they rotate oncall and you'd want to learn their runbooks. Not bravado.
ok. actually can you look at this sentence from the paper I'm citing: they say 'memory is not retrieval'. I keep misquoting it.
I don't have the PDF. If that's a paraphrase, don't put it in quotes. If it's a claim, cite the section, don't decorate it.
section 3. they contrast a store with a pointer. my paragraph currently says we 'retrieve memories like files'.
That's the opposite of their contrast if they mean memory ≠ dumping files. Rewrite your sentence to match section 3 or drop the citation.
I'll rewrite. the draft is a mess.
Which draft — the hiring email or the paragraph that cites section 3?
hm. both. start with the paper one.
Replace 'retrieve like files' with something that admits a pointer/store distinction, then say what *you* do. Don't force their slogan.
need to sort receipts. some of the cafe ones are just me, some were the offsite. I don't want to expense sandwiches I ate alone lol
If the offsite had a calendar invite and a group, keep those. Solo cafe before standup is personal. When unsure, don't expense it.
there's a 14.60 from tuesday with no note. I think that was us
Without a note it's a guess. Ask one person who was there before it hits the report.
later. the tap in the kitchen is dripping again. washer or building?
If it's the spout washer it's a cheap ring. If it's the handle packing, stop tightening and tell the building — you can strip it.
it's the spout I think. also we are leaking the access token in the share URL again, QA sent a screenshot
That's a security bug, not the kitchen. Strip tokens from query strings; use a one-time fragment or a server-side share id.
I thought we did. must be the new share sheet. tokne in the query. typo token.
New share sheet likely copied an old helper. Search `access_token=` and `hashHistory` on that path.
k I'll grep. never mind I'll do it tomorrow, if QA is the only one who saw it
If a token hit a URL it may also have hit logs or referrers. Don't wait on 'only QA' as a threat model.
fine. what did we decide?
About which — email attachment, paper sentence, 14.60 receipt, tap, or the token in the share URL?
cover for the zine. photo or should I draw it. totally different thing sorry
Photo if you already have a strong one; drawing if the issue is handmade on purpose. I wouldn't mix a stock photo with a xerox look.
drawing. ok go back to the draft
Email draft or the citation paragraph? You used 'draft' for both.
the other one
Still two. Last selected in this thread was the zine cover (drawing). 'The other one' from there isn't unique.
the token thing then. not a gift token, the url.
Access token on the new share-sheet query string. Strip it; don't treat it as the expense 'note' or a zine token.
continue where we left off
Last specified was the share URL token. Before that, zine cover = drawing, tap = likely spout washer, receipts = don't guess 14.60.
